prereg_decision_threshold.source: the replication pre-registration — 'THRESHOLD ARITHMETIC RECOMPUTED — RULE UNCHANGED, INPUT CORRECTED', written after generating but BEFORE computing any certification number
prereg_decision_threshold.rule: R1 REPLICATES iff certified accuracy recovers >= 50% of the headroom above the answerer's OWN base rate, AND the exact one-sided binomial test of that slice against the base rate gives p < 0.05
prereg_decision_threshold.answerer: A3 = B1_aug_s0 (sota_push adapter, native 768px, 3220 augmented examples), K=8 majority vote on the same 210 composition-exclusion structures

branches.R1: lift recovers >= 50% of headroom AND p < 0.05 -> certification effect is answerer-independent; report as replicated
branches.R2: lift positive and significant (p < 0.05) but recovers < 50% of headroom -> replicated in DIRECTION but attenuated; state the fraction recovered, do not claim the B1-level effect size generalises
branches.R3: lift not significant (p >= 0.05) or negative -> the B1 result does NOT generalise across answerers; demote certification from a general capability claim to a single-checkpoint observation

prereg_decision_threshold.threshold_rationale: 50% of headroom is chosen because the B1 result recovered 77.1%; a rule at 50% asks the effect to be more than half as strong on a different answerer — a genuine test rather than a formality, without demanding the exact original magnitude on a harder base
secondary_commitments: the OUTCOME chain (B3) must remain NULL on this answerer (p >= 0.05); if B3 certifies A3 the process-vs-outcome contrast is answerer-specific — the sharper falsification test of the two
V2b's false-certification rate (B1: 3/130 = 0.0231) should stay below B3's; a reversal falsifies the error-decorrelation mechanism story
coverage will differ and that is EXPECTED, not a finding
prereg_decision_threshold.note_on_rounding: the record's finding prose quotes this bar as 0.8453; the replication pre-registration computes 0.8452. Same rule, rounding of 0.6905 + 0.15475 = 0.84525.

prereg_decision_threshold_superseded.why: the original pre-registration used base rate 0.6619 from sota_push's K=3 evaluation; the replication runs at K=8, where the same answerer's base rate is 145/210 = 0.6905 (+0.0286). Certification is computed on THOSE generations, so the lift must be measured against THEIR base rate. The RULE is untouched; only its arithmetic input changed. The corrected bar (0.8452) is STRICTER than the 0.8310 implied by the stale input, so the correction cannot be accused of loosening the test.

original_B1_answerer_form.note: this is answerer 1 (B1-direct, K=8, base 0.6143). The 77.1%-of-headroom result is what motivated setting the replication bar at 50%. The same 50%-of-headroom rule applied to this answerer gives 0.8072.

prereg_decision_threshold_superseded.lesson: fix the base rate at the K the experiment will actually use; quoting a base rate from a different decoding budget writes a threshold that does not mean what it says

notes: The verdict in this record is judged against prereg_decision_threshold, which was committed in advance. Without it the verdict is unfalsifiable. lift_vs_base_rate entries in `chains` are computed against the ANSWERER-1 base rate 0.6143; the replication threshold above applies to the A3 answerer at base 0.6905 (see replication.json).
